Everything on this site is free: the book, the exercise books in R, JASP and SPSS, the toys and the tables, the archive. Read it, download it, print it, work through it — that is what it is here for.

## For yourself: go ahead

<!-- BEN: "een psycholoog" staat niet in gebruik.qmd; het komt uit jouw eigen rijtje van 24-10
     ("studenten, mensen, psychologen, ..."). De psycholoog-testlezer: "this isn't student-only, but
     it misses me." En "or you simply want to teach yourself" werd "or you want to teach yourself":
     de gepensioneerde testlezer merkte dat in elk rijtje alleen de niet-professional "simply"
     kreeg. Het Nederlands zegt "of wil je jezelf gewoon statistiek leren". -->
Whether you are a student, a teacher, a psychologist, a researcher, or you want to teach yourself statistics — use what you need. You don't have to ask, and you don't have to give anything back.

## Linking is always fine

<!-- MIEKE: "studiehandleiding" — gekozen "course guide"; alternatief "module handbook" (Brits
     universiteitswoord). -->
<!-- BEN: het Nederlands zegt "je klas, je studenten, een collega ... je studiehandleiding, je
     syllabus, je mail": vier van de zes voorbeelden uit het klaslokaal, terwijl "linken mag altijd"
     voor iedereen geldt. De gepensioneerde testlezer: "I'd share it with my brother-in-law or under
     a Guardian article." Nu eerst wie iedereen heeft, dan de klas. -->
Want to send someone here — a colleague, a friend, your class? Share the link. Put it in an email, a forum post, your course guide or your syllabus. Pointing people here is never something to ask permission for; it is exactly what I hope you will do.

## Degree programmes: please get in touch first

<!-- MIEKE: "elektronische leeromgeving" — gekozen "virtual learning environment" (het Britse
     woord); alternatief "learning platform". -->
If a programme wants to build the material into its teaching — as required reading, in its virtual learning environment, in a course reader, as course material — I would like to hear about it beforehand. Mail me at [vragen@countcamp.org](mailto:vragen@countcamp.org), and we will agree on something that works for both of us.

<!-- MIEKE: "verwijzen" en "opnemen" — gekozen "linking to" en "building in" (Angelsaksisch, en
     het paar blijft een paar). Eerst stond er "pointing to" en "taking in"; Rosie las "taking
     in" als beetnemen. Alternatief: "linking to" en "adopting". -->
The difference is between *linking to* and *building in*: anyone may link to the site, always; making the material itself part of a curriculum starts with a conversation. That goes for the book and for the exercise books alike.

## Support

I build CountCamp in the hours around my paid work. I would much rather work on it full-time — more room simply means more book: chapters that aren't there yet, exercise books that could be better. If you would like to help that along, you can do so here.
